Maya: Nightly sweep flagged a 7-12% tail-latency regression on candidate-k32 for long sequences (seq=4096) on A100-80GB. Perf summary attached.
perf-bot: nightly-sweep/1954321000 - candidate-k32 - A100 - p99 latency +9.8% vs baseline (k16). CI link: https://ci/redwood/1954321000
Alex: hmm. Is kv-cache enabled in that run? That can blow up p99 if cache miss pattern changes.
Maya: KV cache ON. Command used:
```bash
./bench_runner --kernel candidate-k32 --model gpt-large --seq-len 4096 --kv-cache yes --batch 1 --iters 200
```
Maya: Raw tail latencies: [45.2, 47.1, 49.0, 48.8, 52.1] ms (p50/p90/p99) -> 20/41/52 ms
Jun: Can you also run with continuous batching enabled? That interacts with the kernel selection heuristics.
Maya: Running now with `--batching continuous --batch-window-ms 5`.
(Maya: added :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
Maya: With continuous batching: p99 drops to 31 ms. So batching masks something.
Alex: Interesting — maybe candidate-k32's kernel has worse KV cache streaming for single-token micro-ops but benefits from batching. Might cause SLO regressions for chat workloads.
Jun: Suggestion: add a sequence-length-aware gate in autotuner: prefer k16 for seq>=2048 unless batching>1.
Lisa: We should fail the candidate if p99 degrades >5% for any representative workload in the nightly matrix. Current CI threshold is 10%.
Alex: I agree. Lowering to 5% will stop noisy winners. We need to document the matrix: seq lens [64,512,2048,4096], batch [1,4], hw [A100,H100]
perf-bot: triggered rerun for candidate-k32 w/ batching enabled and batching disabled. Started jobs: 1954321011,1954321055
perf-bot: summary: A100 no-batch p99 +10%; A100 batch p99 -3%; H100 both within 2%.
Jun: Could be arch-specific kernel path; k32 uses different instruction mix that underperforms on A100 memory subsystem for long KV strides.
Maya: Captured perf counters: L2_miss_up 1.8e6, DRAM_reads 3.2e6 for A100 no-batch. With batching, L2_miss_up 0.9e6.
Alex: Ok. Action items:
- Maya: add microprobe to isolate KV read pattern (seq=4096, cache warm/cold)
- Jun: prototype seqlen-aware policy in autotuner, add to canary
- Lisa: change nightly gate to p99 5% threshold and add A100/H100 matrix
- @perf-bot: mark candidate-k32 as "needs-gating" until re-eval
Maya: will upload traces and perf profiles to S3: s3://redwood-perf/candidate-k32/1954321000
Alex: also add a smoke test to perf CI that runs `kv-warmup` before the p99 measurement
Jun: we should add a note in the kernel registry: "candidate-k32: prefers batching >=2 or seq <2048 on A100"
Lisa: ok. I'll open the PR to lower the gate and add the matrix.
(Maya: added :white_check_mark:)
ci-bot: candidate-k32 status -> blocked (gating change requested) 1954323120
